guides.title: Getting started
guides.markdown:
# Getting started

AL Loader (Alyn Lua Loader) runs Lua scripts inside ReSA Multiplayer on
Android, iOS and PC. Scripts are plain `.lua` files; the loader uses LuaJIT
(Lua 5.1 with the `ffi` and `bit` libraries).

## Where scripts live

Everything is in the **Mods** tab of the Files screen, in `mods/AL Loader/`:

| Folder | What goes there |
|---|---|
| `scripts/` | Your scripts. Every `.lua` / `.luac` here starts with the game. |
| `lib/` | Libraries scripts `require` (mimgui, samp.events, inicfg, ...). Comes with the app; do not edit, it is replaced on updates. |
| `config/` | Settings files scripts save (inicfg, jsoncfg, mimgui window positions). Made the first time a script saves something. |
| `logs/` | `alloader.log`: what the loader did and every script error. |

A `.lua` dropped straight into `mods/AL Loader/` (not `scripts/`) is **not
loaded**. The launcher offers to move such files for you.

## Your first script

Create `scripts/hello.lua` (the Files tab has New file and an editor):

```lua
script_name("Hello")
script_author("You")

function main()
  -- wait until the player exists
  while not isSampAvailable() do wait(100) end
  sampAddChatMessage("{33AAFF}[Hello]{FFFFFF} AL Loader works!", -1)
  sampRegisterChatCommand("hello", function(arg)
    sampAddChatMessage("Hello " .. (arg ~= "" and arg or "world"), 0xFFFFFFFF)
  end)
  wait(-1) -- keep the script alive
end
```

Start the game, join a server and type `/hello`.

## Turning AL Loader on or off

Settings > AL Loader. With it off nothing is loaded. With no scripts in
`scripts/` it does nothing and costs nothing.

## When something does not work

Open `logs/alloader.log` (or the Script Manager's Log tab). A script that
errors is stopped and the error is written there with the line number.

guides.title: Script structure
guides.markdown:
# Script structure

## Information

Call these at the top of the file. They show in the Script Manager.

```lua
script_name("My script")
script_author("Name")              -- or script_authors("A", "B")
script_version("1.2")
script_version_number(12)
script_description("What it does")
script_url("https://...")
script_dependencies("mimgui", "samp.events")
script_properties("work-in-pause") -- keep running while the game is paused
```

## main and wait

`main()` runs as the script's first coroutine. `wait(ms)` gives the game
control back: `wait(0)` waits one frame, `wait(-1)` sleeps forever (the
script stays loaded and its events and commands keep working).

```lua
function main()
  while true do
    wait(1000)
    print("one second")
  end
end
```

Never loop without `wait`: the game freezes until the loop ends.

## Threads

```lua
local t = lua_thread.create(function(a, b)
  wait(500)
  print(a + b)
end, 1, 2)
-- t:status() -> "running", "suspended", "dead" ...; t:terminate()
```

## Global values

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `PLAYER_PED` | Your character's handle (use it with the `Char` functions). |
| `PLAYER_HANDLE` | Your player handle (the `Player` functions). |
| `AL_VERSION` | Loader version, major*1000000 + minor*1000 + patch. |
| `AL_PLATFORM` | `"android"`, `"ios"` or `"windows"`. |
| `AL_DPI_SCALE` | Screen scale for UI sizes (about 2 on phones, 1 on PC). |
| `MONET_DPI_SCALE`, `MONET_VERSION` | The same two values under MonetLoader's names, so its scripts size their windows correctly. |

## Other scripts

```lua
for _, s in ipairs(script.list()) do print(s.name, s.filename) end
local other = script.find("Chat Log")
if other then other:reload() end
script.load(getWorkingDirectory() .. "/scripts/other.lua")
thisScript():unload()
```

`import("other.lua")` loads another script and returns what it exported
through `EXPORTS`.

## Files and folders

`getWorkingDirectory()` is `mods/AL Loader`; `getGameDirectory()` is the
game files folder. Paths use `/` on every platform. `require "name"`
searches `lib/`, then `scripts/`.

guides.title: Events
guides.markdown:
# Events

Define a global function with the event's name, or register any number of
handlers with `addEventHandler("onTouch", fn)`.

| Event | Arguments | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `onSystemInitialized()` | | All scripts are loaded. |
| `onScriptLoad(script)` | script | Another script was loaded. |
| `onScriptTerminate(script, quitGame)` | script, bool | A script stopped (yours too: compare `script.id == thisScript().id`). |
| `onExitScript(quitGame)` | bool | This script is about to stop. |
| `onQuitGame()` | | The game is closing. |
| `onScriptMessage(text, script)` | string, script | A script printed a line. |
| `onSystemMessage(text, type, script)` | string, int, script | The loader logged a line. |
| `onD3DPresent()` | | Every frame, while drawing is open: put `render*` calls here. |
| `onTouch(type, id, x, y)` | int, int, int, int | A finger: type 1 up, 2 down, 3 move. Return `false` to keep the touch from the game. |
| `onSendRpc(id, bs, priority, reliability, channel)` | | An RPC the client sends. Return `false` to drop it, or new values to change it. |
| `onReceiveRpc(id, bs)` | | An RPC from the server. Return `false` to drop it. |
| `onSendPacket(id, bs, priority, reliability, channel)` | | A packet the client sends (sync data). |
| `onReceivePacket(id, bs)` | | A packet from the server. |

The RakNet events give you a `BitStream`; read it with the
`raknetBitStreamRead*` functions. Most scripts use the **samp.events**
library instead, which decodes every SA-MP RPC into named handlers:

```lua
local sampev = require "samp.events"

function sampev.onServerMessage(color, text)
  if text:find("password") then return false end -- hide the line
end

function sampev.onSendChat(message)
  return { message:upper() } -- change what you send
end
```

Some of its handlers: `onServerMessage`, `onChatMessage`, `onShowDialog`,
`onSendDialogResponse`, `onSendCommand`, `onSendChat`, `onSetPlayerPos`,
`onCreate3DText`, `onShowTextDraw`, `onPlayerJoin`, `onPlayerQuit`. Open
`lib/samp/events.lua` in the Files tab for the full list and argument names.

guides.title: Drawing on screen
guides.markdown:
# Drawing on screen

## render functions

Call them from `onD3DPresent()`, which runs every frame while the frame is
being drawn. Coordinates are screen pixels (`getScreenResolution()`);
colours are `0xAARRGGBB`.

```lua
local font

function onD3DPresent()
  if not font then return end
  local sw, sh = getScreenResolution()
  renderDrawBox(20, sh - 80, 220, 40, 0xAA000000)
  renderFontDrawText(font, "Hello", 30, sh - 70, 0xFFFFFFFF)
end

function main()
  font = renderCreateFont("Arial", 12 * AL_DPI_SCALE, 5) -- 5 = bold + border
  wait(-1)
end
```

Useful: `renderDrawLine`, `renderDrawBoxWithBorder`, `renderDrawPolygon`,
`renderLoadTextureFromFile`, `renderDrawTexture`,
`renderGetFontDrawTextLength`, `renderGetFontDrawHeight`. Text accepts
`{RRGGBB}` colour tags.

## 3D positions on screen

```lua
local x, y, z = getCharCoordinates(ped)
local visible, sx, sy = convert3DCoordsToScreenEx(x, y, z + 1.0, true, true)
if visible then renderDrawLine(sx - 10, sy, sx + 10, sy, 2, 0xFFFF0000) end
```

## Game text

`printString(text, ms)`, `printStringNow`, `printBig(gxt, ms, style)` and the
`displayText*` functions draw the game's own text styles.

`displayText*`, `drawRect` and `drawSprite` use the game's 640x448 script
space, kept 4:3 and centred on wide screens (x = 320 is the middle of the
screen). A script written for a stretched 640x448 screen can
`require "sa_renderfix"` to keep its layout. Call `useRenderCommands(true)`
once before drawing with them: only then does the game clear the list each
frame (128 rectangles and 96 text lines at most).

guides.title: Windows and menus (mimgui)
guides.markdown:
# Windows and menus (mimgui)

`mimgui` is Dear ImGui 1.72 for Lua. Windows react to touch (and mouse and
keyboard on PC); a text field opens the keyboard. A finger that lands on an
AL window does not reach the game.

On PC a window shows the mouse pointer while it is open: the mouse stops
turning the camera, and clicks, hover and the wheel go to the window. An
overlay that should stay on screen without taking the mouse (a HUD) sets
`HideCursor` on the frame `OnFrame` returns:

```lua
local hud = imgui.OnFrame(function() return true end, function() --[[ draw ]] end)
hud.HideCursor = true
```

```lua
local imgui = require "mimgui"
local show = imgui.new.bool(false)
local volume = imgui.new.float(0.5)
local name = imgui.new.char[64]("player")

imgui.OnInitialize(function()
  imgui.GetIO().IniFilename = nil -- do not save window positions
end)

imgui.OnFrame(function() return show[0] end, function()
  imgui.SetNextWindowSize(imgui.ImVec2(300 * AL_DPI_SCALE, 0), imgui.Cond.FirstUseEver)
  imgui.Begin("My window", show)
  imgui.SliderFloat("Volume", volume, 0, 1)
  imgui.InputText("Name", name, 64)
  if imgui.Button("Say hi", imgui.ImVec2(-1, 0)) then
    sampSendChat("hi from " .. require("ffi").string(name))
  end
  imgui.End()
end)

function main()
  while not isSampAvailable() do wait(100) end
  sampRegisterChatCommand("mywin", function() show[0] = not show[0] end)
  wait(-1)
end
```

Values a widget changes are `imgui.new.*` boxes: read them with `[0]`
(`show[0]`), text with `ffi.string(buf)`.

Text functions (`Text`, `TextColored`, `TextWrapped`, `TextDisabled`) are
printf-style: pass text that could contain `%` as an argument,
`imgui.Text("%s", text)`.

Sizes: multiply by `AL_DPI_SCALE` so the window looks the same on a phone
and a monitor. Fonts: `imgui.GetIO().Fonts:AddFontFromFileTTF(path, size)`
inside `OnInitialize`.

Libraries built on mimgui: `notifications` (toast messages), `fAwesome6`
(icons).

guides.title: SA-MP and the server
guides.markdown:
# SA-MP and the server

## Chat and commands

```lua
sampAddChatMessage("{FF8800}Only you see this", -1)
sampSendChat("hello")            -- chat line to the server
sampSendChat("/time")            -- a server command
sampProcessChatInput("/qc")      -- as if typed: other scripts' commands first
sampRegisterChatCommand("cmd", function(arg) ... end)
```

A command you register never reaches the server.

## Players, vehicles and objects

SA-MP ids and game handles are different numbers:

```lua
local ok, myId = sampGetPlayerIdByCharHandle(PLAYER_PED)
for id = 0, sampGetMaxPlayerId() do
  if sampIsPlayerConnected(id) then
    print(id, sampGetPlayerNickname(id), sampGetPlayerPing(id), sampGetPlayerScore(id))
    local found, ped = sampGetCharHandleBySampPlayerId(id) -- streamed in?
  end
end
```

`sampGetCarHandleBySampVehicleId`, `sampGetVehicleIdByCarHandle`,
`sampGetObjectHandleBySampId` convert vehicles and objects.

## Dialogs

```lua
sampShowDialog(9000, "Title", "Line one\nLine two", "OK", "Close", 2) -- 2 = list
-- then poll:
local result, button, list, input = sampHasDialogRespond(9000)
```

`sampIsDialogActive`, `sampGetCurrentDialogId`, `sampGetDialogText` read the
server's dialog; `sampSendDialogResponse(id, button, listitem, input)`
answers it.

## Server

`isSampAvailable()` is true while the client is up: once it starts joining a
server, and for the whole session in offline mode ("Play offline"), so
scripts that wait for it run offline too. Offline there is no server: ids
come back as -1, sends do nothing, `sampAddChatMessage` still prints to the
chat, and a typed or sent `/command` runs the client's own commands and the
ones scripts registered with `sampRegisterChatCommand`.
`sampGetCurrentServerName()`, `sampGetCurrentServerAddress()` (host, port),
`sampGetPlayerCount()`.

## RakNet

Build and send your own packets and RPCs:

```lua
local bs = raknetNewBitStream()
raknetBitStreamWriteInt32(bs, 1)
raknetSendRpc(53, bs)            -- or raknetEmulRpcReceiveBitStream to fake one from the server
raknetDeleteBitStream(bs)
```

Packets and RPCs that pass through can be read, changed or dropped in the
`onSend*` / `onReceive*` events (see Events) or through `samp.events`.
Servers can see what you send: scripts that cheat get you banned.

guides.title: Libraries and saving settings
guides.markdown:
# Libraries and saving settings

`require` loads libraries from `lib/`. The ones that come with AL Loader:

| Library | Use |
|---|---|
| `mimgui` | Windows, buttons, inputs (see Windows and menus). |
| `samp.events` | Named handlers for every SA-MP RPC. |
| `inicfg` | Settings in `.ini` files under `config/`. |
| `jsoncfg` | Settings in `.json` files under `config/`. |
| `encoding` | Text code pages: `encoding.UTF8` / `CP1251` converters. |
| `notifications` | Small toast messages (mimgui). |
| `widgets` | Touch control ids (`WIDGET_ATTACK`, `WIDGET_SAMP_VOICE`, ...) for `isWidgetPressed` and friends. Ids of controls the game never shows are kept and simply never fire. |
| `sa_renderfix` | Makes `drawRect`, `drawSprite` and `displayText*` place things like the PC game (640x448 stretched over the screen) instead of the centred 4:3 area. |
| `fAwesome6` | Icon font for mimgui. |
| `vector3d`, `matrix3x3` | 3D maths. |
| `socket`, `socket.http`, `ltn12`, `copas` | Network: TCP/UDP, HTTP. |
| `cjson`, `encodeJson` / `decodeJson` | JSON. |
| `lfs` | Folders and file attributes. |
| `effil` | Real OS threads (data shared through tables and channels). |
| `md5`, `sha1`, `base64`, `basexx` | Hashes and encodings. |
| `inspect` | Pretty-print a table. |

## Settings

```lua
local inicfg = require "inicfg"
local cfg = inicfg.load({ main = { enabled = true, size = 12 } }, "myscript")
cfg.main.size = 14
inicfg.save(cfg, "myscript") -- config/myscript.ini
```

```lua
local jsoncfg = require "jsoncfg"
local cfg = jsoncfg.load({ list = {} }, "myscript") -- config/myscript.json
jsoncfg.save(cfg, "myscript")
```

## Text code pages

Servers send chat in their own code page (often Windows-1251 for Russian
servers). Convert before showing it in mimgui:

```lua
local encoding = require "encoding"
encoding.default = "CP1251"
local u8 = encoding.UTF8
imgui.Text("%s", u8(text_from_server))
```

guides.title: Bringing scripts from other loaders
guides.markdown:
# Bringing scripts from other loaders

Most MoonLoader and mobile Lua loader scripts run unchanged: the script
functions, events, `samp.events`, mimgui, inicfg and the RakNet functions
have the same names.

What is different, because ReSA is its own engine:

- **No memory or hooks.** `readMemory`, `writeMemory`, `getModuleHandle`,
  hooking libraries and fixed addresses do not exist. Everything goes
  through the functions in this reference. A script that pokes addresses
  needs a rewrite with them.
- **Global names.** Use `AL_VERSION`, `AL_PLATFORM`, `AL_DPI_SCALE` and
  `al_cp1251_to_utf8` / `al_utf8_to_cp1251`. A script that checks another
  loader's version global has to check `AL_VERSION` instead.
- **Folders.** Paths are under `mods/AL Loader`; use
  `getWorkingDirectory()` instead of a fixed folder name.
- **Platforms.** The same script runs on Android, iOS and PC. Check
  `AL_PLATFORM` for anything platform-specific (the `android` library only
  works on Android). On iOS the Lua JIT compiler is off, so very heavy
  loops run slower than on Android or PC.
- **Touch and keyboard.** `onTouch` works everywhere; on PC the mouse comes
  in as touch 0, and text fields take the physical keyboard.
  `isKeyDown(vk)`, `wasKeyPressed(vk)`, `wasKeyReleased(vk)` and
  `isKeyJustPressed(vk)` take Windows virtual-key codes as in MoonLoader
  (`0xC0` is the backtick, `0x41` is A); they work on PC and on phones with
  a keyboard attached. A key typed into an AL text field is not reported.
